READ END TO END (declare full coverage by quoting the first and last non-blank lines of each):
1. ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2025-09-16_information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt — the State's Information, 10 pp., including a probable-cause statement
2. ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/2025-09-16_affidavit-of-probable-cause_dc27880530.txt — the arrest affidavit, 3 pp.

These are ACCUSATORY PLEADINGS in *State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson*, Case No. 251403576. Every factual assertion in them is an ALLEGATION by a party, not a finding. No court has found any of it true.

⚠️ HAZARD 11: these are PDF text extractions and are LINE-WRAPPED. Normalise whitespace before believing any null.

TASK: produce the inventory of MATERIAL content a faithful library summary of these two documents must record. Specifically:
- every CHARGE with its statute, degree, alleged date and the specific conduct alleged;
- every ENHANCEMENT / AGGRAVATING FACTOR and exactly which counts carry it;
- every factual assertion the State makes about the events of 2025-09-10 and the investigation (timeline, surveillance, the rifle and ammunition, the roof, the recovery, the searches);
- every source of information the State names for its allegations (witnesses, agencies, categories of evidence);
- every quoted message or document the State reproduces;
- every internal inconsistency, hedge, or qualifier in the State's own account — including anywhere the two documents differ from each other on the same fact (times, spellings, wording, the number of charges);
- anything the State expressly says is NOT yet known, pending, or unresolved.

For each item: id (M-nn), which document, location landmark, content (≤40 words, quote only short spans), and **materiality: what a reader would get WRONG about these filings if the item were omitted from a summary.** Apply the gate strictly — drop anything whose honest answer is "nothing."

⚠️ CONSTRAINTS, and they are strict:
- **Both documents print the defendant's home address and date of birth. Do NOT reproduce either.** Refer to "the address line" / "the DOB line" if you must reference them at all.
- The documents describe **a private individual's gender identity and a romantic relationship**, and recount statements by **the defendant's mother, father, and a family friend**. Record the EXISTENCE and ARGUMENTATIVE ROLE of that material in the minimum words necessary, attributed to the State. **Do not elaborate it, do not quote it beyond what is strictly needed to say what the State alleges, and name no private individual beyond how the documents themselves refer to them** (the documents use "Robinson's mother", "the roommate", etc. — follow that).
- Never reproduce any contact detail.
- Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and has NOT been bound over. Record allegations as allegations; adopt nothing; make no case-posture statement.

OUTPUT: coverage declaration, then the inventory. COMPACT — at most ~1800 words. Expect 35–60 items.

aggravating factor in their deliberations that the defendant committed a violent criminal offense in 
the presence of a child.
 
COUNT 3: OBSTRUCTION OF JUSTICE, a Second Degree Felony, in violation of Utah 
Code Ann. § 76-8-306(2), in that on September 10, 2025, in Utah County, the defendant, Tyler 
James Robinson, with intent to hinder, delay, or prevent the investigation, apprehension, 
prosecution, conviction, or punishment of any person regarding conduct that constitutes a criminal 
offense: (c) concealed or removed the firearm used to shoot Charlie Kirk; and the conduct that 
constitutes an offense would be a capital felony or first degree felony. 
 
COUNT 4: OBSTRUCTION OF JUSTICE, a Second Degree Felony, in violation of Utah 
Code Ann. § 76-8-306(2), in that on or about September 11, 2025, in Utah County, the defendant, 
Tyler James Robinson, with intent to hinder, delay, or prevent the investigation, apprehension, �

3
prosecution, conviction, or punishment of any person regarding conduct that constitutes a criminal 
offense: (c) destroyed, concealed, or removed the clothing he wore during the shooting; and the 
conduct that constitutes an offense would be a capital felony or first degree felony.
COUNT 5: TAMPERING WITH A WITNESS, a Third Degree Felony, in violation of 
Utah Code Ann. § 76-8-508, in that on or about September 10, 2025, in Utah County, the 
defendant, Tyler James Robinson, (a)(i) believed that an official proceeding or investigation was 
pending or about to be instituted; or (ii) intended to prevent an official proceeding or investigation; 
and (b) attempted to induce or otherwise cause his roommate to (ii) withhold testimony, 
information, a document, or an item, to wit: directing his roommate to delete incriminating text 
messages.
 
COUNT 6: TAMPERING WITH A WITNESS, a Third Degree Felony, in violation of 
Utah Code Ann. § 76-8-508, in that on or about September 11, 2025, in Utah County, the 
defendant, Tyler James Robinson, (a)(i) believed that an official proceeding or investigation was 
pending or about to be instituted; or (ii) intended to prevent an official proceeding or investigation; 
and (b) attempted to induce or otherwise cause his roommate to (ii) withhold testimony or
information, to wit: directing his roommate to stay silent if police questioned the roommate. 
COUNT 7: VIOLENT OFFENSE COMMITTED IN THE PRESENCE OF A CHILD, a 
Class A Misdemeanor, in violation of Utah Code Ann. § 76-3-203.10(2) and § 76-3-
203.14(3)(a)(ii) in that on or about September 10, 2025, in Utah County, the defendant, Tyler 
James Robinson, committed criminal homicide in the physical presence of a child younger than 
14 years old, with knowledge that a child was present and may have seen or heard the commission 
of the criminal homicide. 
VICTIM TARGETING ENHANCEMENT: In violation of Utah Code Ann. § 76-3-203.14(2), 
Tyler James Robinson intentionally selected Charlie Kirk because of Tyler James Robinson’s 
belief or perception regarding Charlie Kirk’s political expression.
PROBABLE CAUSE STATEMENT: Brian Davis of the Utah State Bureau of 
Investigations, having probable cause to believe that the defendant committed the above-listed 
offense(s), submitted the following evidence in support of the filing of this Information:
On September 10, 2025, at approximately 12:23 p.m., Charlie Kirk was shot and killed 
while speaking to a large crowd on the campus of Utah Valley University (UVU) in Orem, Utah. 
(Counts 1 and 2). Police found the suspected murder weapon, a bolt-action .30-06 rifle nearby. 
Over the next approximately 33 hours, police conducted a manhunt for the shooter until the 
evening of September 11, 2025, when Tyler James Robinson surrendered to police at the 
Washington County Sheriff’s Office. DNA consistent with Robinson was found on the rifle’s 
trigger. After shooting Mr. Kirk, Robinson hid the gun (Count 3), discarded the clothing he wore 
when he fired the rifle (Count 4), and told his lover/roommate to delete incriminating text messages �

4
(Count 5) and not to talk to police (Count 6). Children were present at the time of the shooting 
(Count 7).
The Shooting.
Turning Point USA, a non-profit organization founded in 2012 by Charlie Kirk, organized 
a public, outdoor event to be held at noon on September 10, 2025, at UVU. The event was the first 
in a series of similar events to be held at college campuses nationwide. Mr. Kirk is a well-known 
conservative activist, famous for these types of events where he discusses various political issues 
and debates with audience members. His events and comments have garnered a significant number 
of supporters and drawn the ire of many who disagree with his political views.
The event at UVU was announced far in advance and garnered significant publicity and 
interest. Consequently, several hundred people attended. Mr. Kirk was interacting with the crowd 
before the event officially got underway. Then, approximately at noon, Mr. Kirk seated himself 
under a portable canopy behind a table and microphone. He began speaking to the crowd and 
fielding questions from attendees, a format Mr. Kirk commonly used at his events. Mr. Kirk 
allowed his questioners to approach a microphone positioned directly in front of him.
Mr. Kirk’s team members were very close to him on his right and left, as well as some 
behind his canopy and others at various close locations near him. The large crowd surrounded Mr. 
Kirk on three sides. Temporary metal fencing separated attendees from Mr. Kirk by only a matter 
of feet. Directly above and behind Mr. Kirk was the UVU Hall of Flags, an indoor walkway 
spanning several hundred feet with floor-to-ceiling glass windows which overlook the plaza where 
Mr. Kirk was seated. People were in the walkway at the time of the shooting.
Approximately fifteen minutes into the event, Mr. Kirk was answering a question about 
mass shootings by transgender individuals when a gunshot rang out. The bullet struck Mr. Kirk in 
the neck. He slumped to the ground almost immediately. The bullet’s trajectory passed closely to 
several other individuals beside Mr. Kirk, including the questioner who was standing directly in 
front of Mr. Kirk. Children were visible near Mr. Kirk’s stage when he was shot.
Mr. Kirk was rushed to a nearby hospital where he was declared deceased. The Medical 
Examiner’s report is pending.
The UVU Surveillance Investigation.
At the moment of the shot, a UVU police officer (the UVU Officer) was watching the 
crowd from an elevated vantage point. As soon as he heard the shot, he began to scan the area for 
threats. Believing the shot came from a rifle because of its sound, he looked for potential sniper 
positions. He noted a roof area approximately 160 yards away from Mr. Kirk as a potential 
shooting position and rushed there to look for evidence. �

5
The suspected shooting position is adjacent to an open, publicly-accessible walkway. To 
access the suspected location, a person must climb over a railing and then drop to the roof only 
slightly below. The UVU officer climbed over the railing and down onto the roof. He then walked 
to the suspected shooting position and confirmed a clear shooting corridor between the position 
and Mr. Kirk’s seat. He also noticed markings in the gravel rooftop consistent with a sniper having 
lain on the roof – impressions in the gravel potentially left by the elbows, knees, and feet of a 
person in a prone shooting position.
Police reviewed surveillance from the camera covering the roof and discovered that it 
recorded an individual dressed in dark clothing cross the railing from the public walkway and drop 
onto the roof at approximately 12:15 p.m. Although the individual moved out of the camera’s view 
for a short time, the camera again captured the individual running across the roof and then low￾crawling to the area the UVU Officer recognized as where the suspected sniper had dropped into 
a prone shooting position. After a short time, which matches the known time of the shot, the 
individual arose and ran across the roof to the northeast.
This discovery led to an intensive review of UVU surveillance recordings to attempt to 
track and identify the suspect. Surveillance revealed the following. At approximately 11:51 a.m., 
the suspect entered campus from the north. He is seen wearing a black shirt with an American flag 
in its center, a dark baseball cap, and large sunglasses. Throughout the surveillance, the suspect 
keeps his head down and rarely raises his head enough to get a clear image of his face. As he 
proceeds across the campus, he is seen walking with an unusual gait. The suspect walks with very 
little bending in his right leg – consistent with a rifle being hidden in his pants. This unusual gait 
continues until the suspect is seen crossing the railing off the open walkway and onto the roof, 
where he leaves the camera’s view. 
A camera later captures the suspect as he runs across the roof to the suspected shooting 
position. Immediately after the shot was fired, a camera captures the suspect running across the 
roof carrying an item whose shape is consistent with a rifle. The suspect is then seen climbing 
down from the roof. He appears to drop the item he was carrying as he hits the ground in a 
controlled fall. He then picks up the item and runs toward the northeast end of campus. 
Expanded Crime Scene Investigation.
Law enforcement officers followed the suspect’s escape path to the northeast end of 
campus, where they believed the suspect left campus and entered a wooded area. In that wooded 
area, investigators found a bolt-action rifle wrapped in a towel. The rifle contained one spent round 
and three unspent rounds. This is consistent with the facts officers observed at the time of, and 
immediately after the shooting—no shell casings were found on the roof, suggesting a bolt-action
rather than an auto-loading weapon, and only a single round was fired.�

6
Each round in the rifle contained an etched inscription as follows:
Fired cartridge: NoTices Bulge
OWO What’s 
This?
Second cartridge: Hey Facist!
Catch!
[arrow symbols]
Third cartridge: O Bella ciao,
Bella ciao
Bella ciao
Ciao, ciao!

GAY
Lmao
The rifle, ammunition rounds, and towel were sent for forensic processing. DNA consistent 
with Robinson’s was found on the trigger, other parts of the rifle, the fired cartridge casing, two 
of the three unfired cartridges, and the towel. 
Law enforcement was unable to immediately locate the shooter, so they published photos 
of the shooter from the UVU surveillance cameras and asked for the public’s help to identify him. 
Meanwhile, law enforcement continued to try to identify the shooter through other means.
The Washington County Investigation.
On the evening of September 11, 2025, as law enforcement continued their investigation, 
Tyler James Robinson, went to the Washington County Sheriff’s Office with his parents and a 
family friend to turn himself in. 
Robinson’s mother stated the following to police. On September 11, 2025, the day after 
the shooting, Robinson’s mother saw the photo of the shooter in the news and thought the shooter 
looked like her son. Robinson’s mother called her son and asked him where he was. He said he 
was at home sick and that he had also been at home sick on September 10th. Robinson’s mother 
expressed concern to her husband that the suspected shooter looked like Robinson. Robinson’s 
father agreed.�

7
Robinson’s mother explained that over the last year or so, Robinson had become more 
political and had started to lean more to the left – becoming more pro-gay and trans-rights oriented. 
She stated that Robinson began to date his roommate, a biological male who was transitioning 
genders. This resulted in several discussions with family members, but especially between 
Robinson and his father, who have very different political views. In one conversation before the 
shooting, Robinson mentioned that Charlie Kirk would be holding an event at UVU, which 
Robinson said was a “stupid venue” for the event. Robinson accused Kirk of spreading hate.
Robinson’s father reported that when his wife showed him the surveillance image of the 
suspected shooter in the news, he agreed that it looked like their son. He also believed that the rifle 
that police suspected the shooter used matched a rifle that was given to his son as a gift. As a result, 
Robinson’s father contacted his son and asked him to send a photo of the rifle. Robinson did not 
respond. However, Robinson’s father spoke on the phone with Robinson. Robinson implied that 
he planned to take his own life. Robinson’s parents were able to convince him to meet at their 
home.
As they discussed the situation, Robinson implied that he was the shooter and stated that 
he couldn’t go to jail and just wanted to end it. When asked why he did it, Robinson explained 
there is too much evil and the guy [Charlie Kirk] spreads too much hate. They talked about 
Robinson turning himself in and convinced Robinson to speak with a family friend who is a retired 
deputy sheriff. At Robinson’s father’s request, the family friend met with Robinson and his parents 
and convinced Robinson to turn himself in. 
The family friend spoke to police and reported telling Robinson that it would be best if he 
brought all evidence with him to the sheriff’s office to avoid police having to search his parent’s 
home. The family friend also asked Robinson if he had any clothes that were related to what he 
did. Robinson replied that he had disposed of the clothes in different areas.
The Roommate. 
Police interviewed Robinson’s roommate, a biological male who was involved in a 
romantic relationship with Robinson. The roommate told police that the roommate received 
messages from Robinson about the shooting and provided those messages to police. 
On September 10, 2025, the roommate received a text message from Robinson which said,
“drop what you are doing, look under my keyboard.” The roommate looked under the keyboard 
and found a note that stated, “I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk and I’m going to take 
it.” Police found a photograph of this note. 
The following text exchange then took place.�

8

right????”
Robinson: I am still ok my love, but am stuck in orem for a little while longer yet. 
Shouldn’t be long until I can come home, but I gotta grab my rifle still. To

after, but most of that side of town got locked down. Its quiet, almost

Roommate: Why?
Robinson: Why did I do it?
Roommate: Yeah
Robinson: I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can’t be negotiated out. If I am able 
to grab my rifle unseen, I will have left no evidence. Going to attempt to 
retrieve it again, hopefully they have moved on. I haven’t seen anything 
about them finding it.

Robinson: a bit over a week I believe. I can get close to it but there is a squad car

chance it

grandpas rifle … idek if it had a serial number, but it wouldn’t trace to me. 
I worry about prints I had to leave it in a bush where I changed outfits. 
didn’t have the ability or time to bring it with. … I might have to abandon 
it and hope they don’t find prints. how the fuck will I explain losing it to 
my old man. … 
only thing I left was the rifle wrapped in a towel. … 
remember how I was engraving bullets? The fuckin messages are mostly a 
big meme, if I see “notices bulge uwu” on fox new I might have a stroke 
alright im gonna have to leave it, that really fucking sucks. …�

9
judging from today I’d say grandpas gun does just fine idk. I think that 
was a $2k scope ;-;
…
Robinson: delete this exchange
Robinson: my dad wants photos of the rifle … he says grandpa wants to know 
who has what, the feds released a photo of the rifle, and it is very 
unique. Hes calling me rn, not answering.
…
Robinson: since trump got into office [my dad] has been pretty diehard maga.
…
Robinson: Im gonna turn myself in willingly, one of my neighbors here is a 
deputy for the sheriff.
Robinson: you are all I worry about love
Roommate: I’m much more worried about you
Robinson: don’t talk to the media please. don’t take any interviews or make 
any comments. … if any police ask you questions ask for a lawyer 
and stay silent
The Search of Robinson’s Residence.
Police executed a search warrant on Robinson’s residence. During that search, police 
discovered a shell casing with etchings like the etchings found on the shells in the rifle near 
UVU. Police also found several targets with bullet holes in Robinson’s home. 
Count 1: Aggravated Murder pertains to Robinson’s shooting and killing of Charlie Kirk in a 
manner that exposed others, in addition to Mr. Kirk, to a great risk of death. 
Count 2 Felony Discharge of a Firearm pertains to Robinson’s shooting toward Mr. Kirk, 
knowing that doing so would endanger those in the bullet’s path. The shot caused serious bodily 
injury to Mr. Kirk, ultimately resulting in his death.
Count 3: Obstructing Justice pertains to Robinson’s removal and hiding of the rifle he used to 
shoot Mr. Kirk. 
Count 4: Obstructing Justice pertains to Robinson’s removal and hiding of the clothing he wore 
when he shot Mr. Kirk.
Count 5: Witness Tampering pertains to Robinson’s statement to his roommate telling his 
roommate to delete their text exchange that followed the shooting.
Count 6: Witness Tampering pertains to Robinson’s statement to his roommate telling the 
roommate, “if any police ask you questions ask for a lawyer and stay silent.”�

10
Count 7: Violence Offense Committed in the Presence of a Child pertains to Robinson’s shooting 
of Mr. Kirk in the presence of children under the age of 14 who were visible at the event.
Based upon evidence received from Brian Davis of the Utah State Bureau of Investigations, I 
have reason to believe the defendant committed the offense(s) as charged herein.
Authorized for presentment and filing on September 16, 2025.
UTAH COUNTY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE

Center building. At approximately 1215 hours, Suspect was observed walking up the

## COVERAGE DECLARATION

**Doc A — Information (`…information-charging-document_dc27880532.txt`, 344 lines, 10 printed pp.), read end to end.**
First non-blank line: `1` (page number); first substantive: `JEFFREY S. GRAY # 5852`. Last non-blank line: `Utah County Attorney`.

Both docs are accusatory pleadings; every item below is an **allegation**. Address/DOB lines present in both; not reproduced.

## INVENTORY

**Charges (Doc A)**
- **M-01** | A | Count 1 | Aggravated Murder, **Capital Felony**, §76-5-202, 9/10/2025; intentionally/knowingly caused Kirk's death under circumstance "(iii)… knowingly created a great risk of death to another individual." → Omitting the (iii) subsection loses the *only* aggravator making it capital.
- **M-02** | A | after Count 1 | NOTICE: may carry death penalty, or per §76-3-207.7 LWOP or 25-to-life. → The filing's stated punishment exposure.
- **M-03** | A | Count 2 | Felony Discharge of a Firearm Causing Serious Bodily Injury, F1, §76-11-210(2),(3)(c), 9/10/2025; discharge toward Kirk knowing he may be endangered; caused serious bodily injury.
- **M-04** | A | Count 3 | Obstruction of Justice, F2, §76-8-306(2), 9/10/2025; "(c) concealed or removed the firearm."
- **M-05** | A | Count 4 | Obstruction, F2, same statute, **on or about 9/11/2025**; "destroyed, concealed, or removed the clothing." → Different date from Count 3; the two obstruction counts are not duplicative.
- **M-06** | A | Count 5 | Witness Tampering, F3, §76-8-508, on or about 9/10/2025; directing the roommate to delete incriminating text messages.
- **M-07** | A | Count 6 | Witness Tampering, F3, §76-8-508, on or about 9/11/2025; directing the roommate to stay silent if questioned.
- **M-08** | A | Count 7 | Violent Offense Committed in the Presence of a Child, **Class A Misdemeanor**, §76-3-203.10(2) and §76-3-203.14(3)(a)(ii); homicide in physical presence of a child under 14, with knowledge. → Charged as a standalone count, not only an enhancement.

**Enhancements / aggravators (Doc A) — count-specific**
- **M-09** | A | under Counts 1, 2, 7 | Victim Targeting Enhancement, §76-3-203.14(2): selected Kirk because of Robinson's "belief or perception regarding Charlie Kirk's political expression." → Attaches to exactly three counts; not to 3–6.
- **M-10** | A | under Counts 1, 2 only | "Violent offense committed in the presence of a child" aggravating-factor block. → Not attached to Count 7 (there it is the offense) nor to 3–6.
- **M-11** | A | Counts 1, 2 | NOTICE paragraph on trier-of-fact finding beyond reasonable doubt; **Count 7's enhancement carries no such NOTICE**. → A drafting asymmetry inside the same document.

**Facts alleged — the shooting (Doc A §"The Shooting")**
- **M-12** | A | PC opening | Shot ~12:23 p.m., 9/10/2025, UVU Orem, before a large crowd; bolt-action .30-06 found "nearby." → "Nearby" is the State's own loose framing; the rifle was recovered off the escape route (M-27).
- **M-13** | A | PC opening | "approximately 33 hours" manhunt until evening 9/11, when Robinson **surrendered** at Washington County Sheriff's Office. → The State alleges voluntary surrender, not capture.
- **M-14** | A | ¶TPUSA | TPUSA founded 2012 by Kirk; event announced far in advance; first of a nationwide campus series; several hundred attended. → Establishes foreseeability/publicity, part of the premeditation theory.
- **M-15** | A | ¶layout | Kirk seated ~noon under portable canopy; team members close on both sides and behind; crowd on three sides; temporary metal fencing "only a matter of feet" away. → The crowd-density basis for "great risk of death."
- **M-16** | A | ¶layout | "Hall of Flags" indoor glass walkway spanning several hundred feet directly above and behind Kirk; **people were in the walkway at the time**. → Additional persons in the bullet's line; separate from the crowd.
- **M-17** | A | ¶shot | "Approximately fifteen minutes into the event," Kirk was answering a question about mass shootings by transgender individuals when the shot rang out; struck in the neck; slumped almost immediately. → The State itself supplies the question topic.
- **M-18** | A | ¶shot | Trajectory "passed closely to several other individuals," including the questioner directly in front. → Carries Counts 1(iii) and 2.
- **M-19** | A | ¶shot | "Children were visible near Mr. Kirk's stage." → Sole factual support for Count 7; note "visible," not identified.
- **M-20** | A | end ¶shot | **"The Medical Examiner's report is pending."** → The State expressly concedes cause of death is not yet documented.

**Facts alleged — surveillance/roof (Doc A)**
- **M-21** | A | ¶UVU Officer | An unnamed "UVU Officer" at an elevated vantage point inferred a rifle from the sound, identified a roof "approximately 160 yards away," and went there. → The only distance figure in either document; the roof was found by inference, not by trace.
- **M-22** | A | ¶roof access | Access requires climbing a railing off a public walkway and dropping to a roof "only slightly below." → Alleged public accessibility of the position.
- **M-23** | A | ¶roof | Officer confirmed a "clear shooting corridor"; noted gravel markings "consistent with" a prone shooter — impressions "**potentially** left by the elbows, knees, and feet." → Double hedge; not forensic identification.
- **M-24** | A | ¶roof camera | Individual in dark clothing crossed the railing **~12:15 p.m.**, left camera view briefly, then ran and low-crawled to the position; "After a short time, **which matches the known time of the shot**," rose and ran northeast. → No camera captures the shot itself; the link is timing.
- **M-25** | A | ¶tracking | ~11:51 a.m. suspect entered campus from the north: black shirt with American flag in its centre, dark cap, large sunglasses; head kept down, face rarely clear. → The State concedes no clear facial image.
- **M-26** | A | ¶gait | Unusual gait, "very little bending in his right leg — **consistent with a rifle being hidden in his pants**," ending when he crosses onto the roof. → An inference, expressly labelled as consistency.
- **M-27** | A | ¶escape | Camera shows suspect running with an item "whose shape is consistent with a rifle"; climbs down, appears to drop it in a controlled fall, picks it up, runs northeast.

**Facts alleged — recovery and forensics (Doc A)**
- **M-28** | A | ¶Expanded Crime Scene | Escape path followed to NE campus into a **wooded area**; bolt-action rifle found wrapped in a towel; one spent, three unspent rounds.
- **M-29** | A | same | "no shell casings were found on the roof, suggesting a bolt-action rather than an auto-loading weapon, and only a single round was fired." → The State's own reasoning chain, expressly inferential.
- **M-30** | A | ¶inscriptions | Four engraved rounds quoted: fired — "NoTices Bulge / OWO What's / This?"; "Hey Facist! / Catch!" + arrows; "O Bella ciao…"; "If you Read / This, You Are / GAY / Lmao". → Verbatim text; spellings differ from Doc B (M-47).
- **M-31** | A | ¶forensics | Rifle, rounds, towel sent for processing; DNA "**consistent with** Robinson's" on trigger, other rifle parts, the fired casing, **two of the three** unfired cartridges, and the towel. → Both the qualifier and the 2-of-3 limit; the PC opening states only "trigger."
- **M-32** | A | ¶public appeal | Photos published, public help sought, other identification efforts continued. → Explains how the mother came to see the image.
- **M-33** | A | ¶Search | Search warrant executed at Robinson's residence: a shell casing with etchings "like" those on the shells near UVU, and several targets with bullet holes. → The only alleged physical link at the residence; "like," not matched.

**Named sources of information**
- **M-34** | A | PC caption + closing | Affiant **Brian Davis, Utah State Bureau of Investigations**; Information sworn to by Utah County Attorney **Jeffrey S. Gray**; five named deputy county attorneys; authorized for filing **September 16, 2025**. → Doc A is second-hand from Davis by its own terms.
- **M-35** | B | l.16–18 | Sources: "police officers, multiple video recordings posted on **social media** websites, UVU campus surveillance cameras and those who witnessed the incident." → Doc A names no social-media or witness sourcing.
- **M-36** | A/B | throughout | Persons the State relies on: Robinson's mother, Robinson's father, a family friend (retired deputy sheriff), the roommate, an unnamed UVU officer, an unnamed "family member" (B). → The account is largely family- and roommate-derived.
- **M-37** | B | l.98–99 | Information relayed to Utah County Sheriff's Office, UVU scene investigators, **and the FBI**. → Only mention of federal involvement.

**Family and roommate material (recorded minimally, as the State's allegations)**
- **M-38** | A | ¶mother | The State recounts the mother saying she recognised the published photo as her son; she called him and he said he was home sick on 9/11 and had been home sick 9/10. → An alleged false alibi.
- **M-39** | A | ¶mother | The State uses the mother's account of Robinson's political shift, and of his relationship with the roommate — a biological male transitioning genders — as **motive framing** and as family-friction context with his father. → Records that the State put a private individual's gender identity and the relationship into the pleading for motive; a summary that omits this hides the State's own motive theory. No further detail warranted.
- **M-40** | A | ¶mother | Before the shooting Robinson said Kirk's UVU event was a "stupid venue" and accused Kirk of spreading hate. → Alleged pre-offence statement; the only quoted pre-9/10 words.
- **M-41** | A | ¶father | Father agreed the image looked like their son; believed the suspected rifle matched **a rifle given to his son as a gift**; asked for a photo; no response; on a call Robinson implied he planned to take his own life; parents got him to their home.
- **M-42** | A | ¶father | At the home Robinson "implied that he was the shooter," said he couldn't go to jail and wanted to end it, and when asked why said "there is too much evil and the guy… spreads too much hate." → Implied, not stated — the State's own wording.
- **M-43** | A | ¶family friend | The friend (retired deputy sheriff) told police he advised bringing all evidence to avoid a search of the parents' home, and asked about clothes "related to what he did"; Robinson said he had **disposed of the clothes in different areas**. → Sole support for Count 4.
- **M-44** | A | ¶roommate + exchange | The roommate provided messages; 9/10 text "drop what you are doing, look under my keyboard"; note read "I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk and I'm going to take it." **"Police found a photograph of this note."** → The State has an image, not the note.
- **M-45** | A | quoted exchange, pp.7–9 | Long verbatim exchange reproduced, including admissions ("I am, I'm sorry"), planning "a bit over a week," the drop point/bush, "grandpas rifle," "$2k scope," "engraving bullets," "delete this exchange," intent to surrender to a deputy neighbour, and "if any police ask you questions ask for a lawyer and stay silent." → Direct support for Counts 3–6; a summary must record that the State quotes it, **and that the quotation is punctuated by the State's own ellipses** — it is not continuous.

**Doc B — its own allegations, where they add or differ**
- **M-46** | B | header table | Only **three** offences: Aggravated Murder §76-5-202 **F1**, Felony Discharge F1, Obstruction §76-8-306(2)+(3A) F2 — all with **Offense Date 09/12/2025**, arrest 09/12/2025 04:00. → Charge count (3 v 7), degree (F1 v Capital) and offence date (arrest date v 9/10) all differ from Doc A.
- **M-47** | B | l.86–90 | Inscriptions rendered "Notices **Buldge** OWO what's this?", "hey **fascist**! CATCH!" with up/right/three-down arrows, etc., and described as on **casings found with the rifle**. → Spelling and arrow detail differ from Doc A; Doc A says the rounds were *in* the rifle.
- **M-48** | B | l.83–84 | Rifle identified as a **Mauser Model 98, .30-06, with scope**. → Doc A never names make/model.
- **M-49** | B | l.34–35, 70–71 | The building is named: **Losee Center**; courtyard to its west, roof overlooks it. → Doc A never names the Losee Center.
- **M-50** | B | l.37–43 | Fuller suspect description: white male, dark hair, **long sleeve** shirt with flag **and an eagle**, dark jeans, white/grey Converse-style shoes, **dark backpack**. → Doc A omits eagle, shoes, backpack.
- **M-51** | B | l.46–57 | Timeline: ~1150 grassy area north of Campus Drive at ~800 West; ~1153 pause at tunnel stairs, apparent **cellphone** from right pocket; ~1202 north side of Losee; **entered the Losee Center building** through SE-corner doors. → Doc A has none of this, and never places the suspect inside a building.
- **M-52** | B | l.59–69 | ~1215 up the stairs to the common area; **~1217** climbed the short concrete wall and crouched; ~1222 ran (limp "**absent**"), scooted, lay prone facing west; ~1223 shot. → Roof-entry time conflicts with Doc A's "approximately 12:15 p.m."; the vanished limp is Doc B's own observation.
- **M-53** | B | l.73–80 | ~1223 stood and sprinted north; at the NE corner **placed a dark colored item on the rooftop**, then lowered himself and dropped to the grass; ~1224 crossed Campus Drive; "Suspect appeared to be carrying an item, **whose identity is not clear from the surveillance**." → Directly conflicts with Doc A's "drops the item… in a controlled fall" and with Doc A's "shape is consistent with a rifle."
- **M-54** | B | l.91–94 | **Shoe impression** at the NE rooftop edge consistent with Converse/Chuck Taylor sole. → Absent from Doc A; the only impression evidence tied to footwear.
- **M-55** | B | l.100–106 | Robinson allegedly arrived at UVU in a **grey Dodge Challenger ~08:29 on 9/10**, in a maroon t-shirt, light shorts, black hat with white logo, light shoes; when encountered in Washington County early 9/12 he was "in consistent clothing with the surveillance images." → A second, differently-dressed appearance hours before the shooting, absent from Doc A; the "consistent clothing" claim is unspecific as to which images.
- **M-56** | B | l.107–113 | An unnamed "family member" interview: Robinson more political in recent years; a pre-9/10 dinner where he mentioned Kirk coming to UVU; "The family member also stated Kirk was full of hate" — attribution ambiguous as written; confirmed the grey Challenger. → Doc A attributes the "spreading hate" characterisation to Robinson; Doc B's sentence attributes it to the family member.
- **M-57** | B | l.95–99 | Sequence: a **family member reached out to a family friend**, who contacted WCSO, reporting Robinson "had confessed to them **or implied** that he had committed the incident." → Order of contact differs from Doc A (father asks the friend to come); "confessed or implied" is a hedge.

- **M-60** | B | l.150–154 | Affiant's conclusion covers only aggravated murder, felony discharge, and obstruction "for moving and hiding the rifle" — **no witness tampering, no child-presence count, and no DNA anywhere in Doc B**. → Doc B predates the DNA results and the tampering theory.

**Internal inconsistencies, nulls, and artefacts**
- **M-61** | A | Count 7 mapping ¶, p.10 | Heading reads "**Violence** Offense Committed in the Presence of a Child" (elsewhere "Violent"); Count 3 cites §76-8-306(2) where Doc B cites (2)+(3A). → Citation/label variance within the State's own filings.

- **M-63** | A | caption block | **Case No., Judge, BAIL and SID are blank**; OTN 70090584 (matches Doc B). → The artefact is the as-presented Information, without case-number assignment.

- **M-65** | B | submission block, l.123–143 | "Arrest Date/Time: **NONE**" and blank SID/FBI ID/officer-agency fields, contradicting the document's own "On 09/12/2025 04:00 the defendant was arrested"; PC entered 09/12/2025 07:18; PC IDs "UTBDAVIS – Brian Davis" and "UT018015A – **Attorney General**" (Doc A places Davis at the State Bureau of Investigations); booking agency Utah County Sheriff Office, ORI UT0250000. → Unresolved fields and an agency-attribution difference for the same affiant.
- **M-66** | B | l.57/59, 121/144 | Extraction duplicates one sentence and splits another around the submission block. → A summary must not read these as two separate observations; they are one.
